name: Propranolol
route_note: oral tablets, extended-release capsules and solution; IV for arrhythmias

discovery.by: James Black and colleagues, ICI Pharmaceuticals
discovery.note: Designed to block cardiac beta-receptors to reduce myocardial oxygen demand in angina; succeeded pronethalol.

tagline: The first successful beta-blocker, from angina to migraine and infant haemangiomas
summary: Propranolol is a non-selective beta-blocker developed by James Black, who received a Nobel Prize partly for this work. It is used for hypertension, angina, arrhythmias, migraine prevention, essential tremor, thyrotoxicosis symptoms and, in a paediatric formulation, infantile haemangioma.
mechanism: Propranolol competitively blocks β1-adrenoceptors in the heart, lowering heart rate, contractility and AV conduction and so reducing myocardial oxygen demand. It also reduces renin release from the kidney.

Blockade of β2-receptors can cause bronchoconstriction and blunts hypoglycaemia warning signs. As a lipophilic drug it enters the brain, which may contribute to its effects on migraine, tremor and anxiety symptoms, as well as fatigue and vivid dreams.
uses: Atrial fibrillation rate control and other arrhythmias

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: James Black's team at ICI makes propranolol.

history.title: UK launch
history.detail: Marketed as Inderal in the United Kingdom.

history.title: BHAT
history.detail: The Beta-Blocker Heart Attack Trial shows reduced mortality after myocardial infarction.

history.title: Nobel Prize
history.detail: James Black shares the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, partly for developing propranolol.

history.title: Haemangioma discovery
history.detail: French physicians report by chance that propranolol shrinks infantile haemangiomas.

history.title: Hemangeol
history.detail: The FDA approves an oral solution for proliferating infantile haemangioma.

safety.boxed_warning: Abrupt cessation can exacerbate angina and precipitate myocardial infarction or ventricular arrhythmias in ischaemic heart disease; taper over 1–2 weeks.

facts: It is used off-label for performance anxiety, and its use is banned in some precision sports by WADA.
Overdose can be severe because of sodium-channel blocking (membrane-stabilising) effects.

references.title: Léauté-Labrèze C et al. Propranolol for severe hemangiomas of infancy. N Engl J Med 2008
